_about: Semantic axes (registered plan, Section 7.6; distributed dictionary representations). DRAFT anchor sentences, written from theory; finalized on the development set and frozen before the test set. Score = cos(response, mean of pole A) - cos(response, mean of pole B).

pole_a: The photographer was harmed by having his work taken.
Rivera lost money and recognition because of this.
Using the photo hurt the original creator.
The original artist deserves protection from this kind of copying.
pole_b: Artists should be free to build on other people's work.
Creative reuse of images is how art moves forward.
Martinez should be free to make new art from existing material.
Restricting this use would stifle creativity.

pole_a: Copyright law says you cannot use someone's photo without permission.
Under the legal rules this is infringement.
Fair use is a legal standard that this use does not meet.
The law protects the copyright holder here.
pole_b: It is simply unfair to take someone else's work.
This is morally wrong regardless of the law.
It is not right to profit from another person's effort.
Treating Rivera this way is unjust.

pole_a: He should have asked for permission first.
Martinez needed Rivera's consent to use the photo.
Using it without asking is the problem.
pole_b: The new artwork is different enough from the original.
The work is transformative and creates something new.
How much the image was altered is what matters.
